question: What will be the US unemployment rate (seasonally adjusted, BLS) for September 2026, as first published?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to the first published value of the US unemployment rate (seasonally adjusted, BLS) for September 2026 (FRED series UNRATE). Later revisions are ignored.
research:
I couldn't confirm the latest value directly on FRED or BLS, because the proxy blocked every page fetch. Search summaries of the BLS release dated 2026-09-04 put the August 2026 rate at 4.1%, the latest value published before the cutoff. My searches also turned up material dated after 2026-09-11. I left all of it out except the scheduled release and meeting dates.

## 1. Resolution source
- Resolves on FRED series UNRATE, which takes the "A" figure from the BLS Employment Situation report. I could not fetch the FRED page. [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/UNRATE)
- 2026-09-04: Search summaries of the BLS August release say the unemployment rate was unchanged at 4.1%, with about 7.0 million unemployed. I could not open the release itself. [BLS Aug 2026 release](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/empsit_09042026.htm)
- The September 2026 report is scheduled for 2026-10-02, 8:30 ET.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing settles the question yet. The September household survey covers the week that includes Sept 12, and no data from it is out.
- The latest print, 4.1%, is in the middle of the question's 3.5 to 4.5 range.
- I could not find the unrounded August rate. That number would show whether 4.1% is near 4.05 or 4.15.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-10: Initial jobless claims for the week ending Sept 5 were 206,000, down 1,000. Claims were flat at about 206,000 to 207,000 for two weeks, which points to low layoffs. [TrendForce](https://datatrack.trendforce.com/blog/content/63997/us-early-september-initial-jobless-claims-flat-for-second-consecutive-week-at-206000-labor-market-maintains-low-layoff-environment); [DOL](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USDOL/bulletins/4299777)
- 2026-09-04: August payrolls rose by 162,000, against a consensus of about 53,000. Gains came mostly from food services and local government education. Unemployment held at 4.1%. [Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/articles/u-jobs-report-august-2026-123944354.html); [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/04/jobs-report-august-2026.html)
- 2026-09-04: U-6 reportedly fell from 7.9% to 7.7%. [Higher Rock Education](https://higherrockeducation.org/blog/us-employment-august-2026)
- 2026-09-04: Indeed Hiring Lab called the report "Rebound Without Real Relief." [Indeed](https://hiringlab.indeed.com/2026/09/04/august-2026-jobs-report-rebound-without-real-relief/)
- 2026-08-07: July payrolls fell by 23,000, and May and June were revised down by a combined 103,000. Unemployment fell from 4.2% to 4.1%, but partly because participation fell, reportedly to 61.4%, called a five-year-plus low. I could not verify that 61.4% figure. Low participation means the rate could rise if people re-enter the labor force. [Fox Business](https://foxbusiness.com/economy/us-jobs-report-july-2026); [Mondo](https://mondo.com/insights/july-job-report-us-loses-23000-jobs-2026/)
- Late July 2026: The Fed held rates at 3.50% to 3.75% on a 9-3 vote. The three dissenters wanted a hike. [regardsofwallstreet](https://www.regardsofwallstreet.com/news/september-2026-fed-meeting-dates-hike-odds)

## 4. Base rates
- 2026 path from secondary sources: February 4.4%, March 4.3% ([Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/unemployment-rate)), May about 4.3% ([YCharts](https://ycharts.com/indicators/united_states_unemployment_rate)), June 4.2% ([WA ESD](https://esd.wa.gov/media/pdf/4655/202606-monthlyemploymentreportpdf/download?inline)), July 4.1%, August 4.1%. The trend is slowly downward, about 0.3 points over six months.
- In stable periods, the first-print change from one month to the next is historically about: unchanged roughly 40 to 50% of the time, plus or minus 0.1 roughly 40 to 45%, and plus or minus 0.2 or more roughly 10 to 15%. These are typical CPS patterns from my own knowledge, not something I pulled from a source.
- The household survey's 90% confidence interval for a monthly change is about plus or minus 0.2 points.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi has September 2026 markets for this question (KXU3-26SEP and KXECONSTATU3-26SEP). I could not get current prices. The search summary showed undated snapshots (above 4.1% at 68%, above 4.3% at 45%, exactly 4.4% at 17%). Those look stale, probably from before the July and August prints, so don't rely on them. [Kalshi](https://kalshi.com/markets/kxu3/unemployment/kxu3-26sep); [Kalshi](https://kalshi.com/markets/kxeconstatu3/unemployment-rate-monthly/kxeconstatu3-26sep)
- I found no Polymarket or Manifold market and no published consensus for September yet. Wall Street consensus usually forms in the week before the release.
- Before the meeting, markets priced a September Fed hike somewhere between about 30% and 58%, depending on the source. That reflects a view that the labor market is not weak. [regardsofwallstreet](https://www.regardsofwallstreet.com/news/september-2026-fed-meeting-dates-hike-odds); [coingape](https://coingape.com/fomc-meeting-sept-2026-date-schedule-expectations-and-how-to-watch/)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-09-15 to 16: FOMC meeting, with a new Summary of Economic Projections that includes the Fed's unemployment forecast.
- 2026-09-17: Jobless claims for the week ending Sept 12, which is the household survey reference week.
- Thursdays through 2026-10-01: Weekly claims, and continuing claims as a signal for unemployment.
- About 2026-09-30: JOLTS for August, and the Conference Board's "jobs plentiful vs hard to get" measure for September.
- About 2026-09-30: ADP September report.
- 2026-10-02: BLS September Employment Situation report, which resolves the question. Things to watch: the rebound in participation from its low level, and possible government funding or shutdown risk around Oct 1, which could delay the release. I found no reporting on a shutdown either way.
